items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: I was with one of the first integrated bands in the country. The first one was... by a fine band leader called Boyd Raeburn.

ctx.x: You started at six o’clock. How late did you have to play then?
Well during those days, when you say how late did you have to play, there wasn’t any unions, there wasn’t any days off, there wasn’t any vacation. When I first came to New © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

York there wasn’t any vacations, there wasn’t any unions or anything like that. As a matter of fact, I marched for the day off. I marched for unions, and at that particular time 802 was always — it wasn’t segregated — but it was like uptown, downtown you know. The majority of the black musicians hung out at a place called The Rhythm Club downtown, and the white musicians were on the floor. But for just one reason I hung out downtown, and I would say since I’m interviewing you, I would say that if you look it up,…
